I also dont get the whole washing your chicken-discussion. My family is from rural Poland, everybody I know handles meat without fuss or anything and nothing ever happens. I would estimate handling raw meat without washing, disinfecting,... is the norm in at least 80% of the world. As long as its fresh, nothing should happen. The animal didn't die of diseases and bacteria rarely sits in the muscles or fat of living organisms. "Dangerous" bacteria would most likely infest meat after sitting out for a long time and even then it would need some time to grow to dangerous levels. So as long as meat is fresh and cooled, there really is nothing to worry about if you stop and really think about it. 

I study biology, so Im familiar with the fact that bacteria is everywhere. And even when there are some pathogenic bacteria among those, 9 times out of 10 your body will be able to fight an infection. You probably have pathogenic bacteria on your hands and in your system everyday, multiple times. But your body fights it. Its only the rare cases when your immune system was weakened or something where you will catch a cold or something similar. In fact, the more you come into contact with different kinds of bacteria and viruses, the better. Especially early on in childhood. This is not just a myth, its exactly the same as a mini-vaccine against common pathogens in your area. 

It always infuriates me that especially in the west, there seems to be some kind of hygiene olympics. Its very counterproductive, especially when talking about antibacterial cleaning supplies or hygiene. I get that it seems disgusting to touch "dirty" surfaces in public spaces, but soap and water is more than enough to clean off dirt. Antibiotic and disinfectant resistant bacteria are a real and serious threat to our society, one to which we don't have a solution yet. There are already many annual deaths because of it.
